title: Why Do We Sleep?
paragraphs: We spend about a third of our lives asleep, so it is natural to ask why sleep is so important. Health experts recommend that most adults sleep between seven and nine hours a night, while children and teenagers need more.

Sleep is not one long, flat state. During the night we move through several cycles, each lasting roughly ninety minutes. A cycle includes light sleep, deep sleep and REM sleep, the stage in which most vivid dreams happen.

Each stage has a job. In deep sleep, the body repairs tissue and the brain strengthens the memories it collected during the day. Research also suggests that the brain removes waste products while we sleep, which may help to protect it over time.

A short night now and then is not dangerous, but regular lack of sleep has real effects. People who sleep too little find it harder to concentrate and make decisions, and their mood often suffers. Good sleep, in other words, is part of staying healthy, not a waste of time.
